memos.headline: S07 at 52-week high leads momentum; S04 in structural downtrend remains weakest name in universe
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation across the universe this week. S07 is sitting at its 52-week high with zero drawdown, +61.2% over 26 weeks, and +26.3% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — this is the strongest trend in the group, though at +41.3% above the 200d mean it is extended and I would tighten stops below 720. S03 and S06 are showing strong 4-week momentum (+13.8% and +9.5% respectively) with positive relative strength, but S03's RSI at 71.5 and +11.7% above the 50d mean flags near-term overbought risk. On the other side, S04 is deeply broken: -31.6% from its 52-week high, -21.8% below the 200d mean, RSI 38.3, and -19.1% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks — I see no reason to step in front of that trend until it reclaims at least 400. S01 is quietly deteriorating, trading 5.1% below its 50d and 4.3% below its 200d with negative 4-week relative strength, warranting caution.

views.note: At 52-week high with dominant relative strength (+26.3% vs SPY 12w) and powerful trend; would reassess on a close below 720.
Structural downtrend with -31.6% drawdown, deeply below both moving averages, and terrible relative strength; no buy signal until a sustained close above 400.
Healthy uptrend with +9.5% 4-week return, +7.5% relative strength vs SPY, RSI 65.7 not yet overbought, and low ATR of 2.30%; would cut below 290.
Impressive 4-week surge of +13.8% but RSI 71.5 and +11.7% above 50d mean suggest near-term pullback risk; wait for a retest of 220 to add.
Below both 50d and 200d averages with -5.6% 4-week relative strength vs SPY and RSI 44.3; trend is negative until price reclaims 150.
Strong 12w and 26w returns (+20.5%, +37.0%) but short-term weakness with -5.1% last week, RSI 41.6, and 4.04% ATR making it volatile; need to hold 145 support.
Quietly above both moving averages with +3.6% 12-week relative strength vs SPY and moderate RSI 61.3; would exit below 180.
Sharp 4-week bounce of +9.8% but still -49.2% from 52-week high and below 200d mean; this looks like a bear-market rally until proven otherwise above 320.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Show Exceptional Earnings Power; S02 and S09 Flash Red on Margin Collapse
memos.body: I see a stark bifurcation in this universe between durable high-margin compounders and names where cash-flow quality is deteriorating fast. S10 stands out with 63.1% net margins, 73.2% YoY revenue growth, and near-doubled net income on only $8.47B of total debt — this is the cleanest earnings profile in the group. S04 is similarly compelling at 47.3% net margins with net income up 59.5% YoY on $81.27B of revenue, though $40.26B in debt warrants monitoring. On the other side, S02 is alarming: revenue grew 12.3% but net income collapsed 99.8% to essentially zero, implying massive cost or impairment issues that need explanation before I'd touch it. S09 also concerns me with revenue declining 1.3% and net income falling 14.6% on a thin 7.9% margin, while carrying $34.24B in debt — any further top-line erosion compresses earnings materially.

views.note: 63.1% net margin, 73.2% revenue growth, 94.5% net income growth, and minimal leverage at $8.47B debt — best earnings quality in the universe.
47.3% net margin with 59.5% net income growth on 16.7% revenue growth demonstrates powerful operating leverage; would revisit if debt rises above $50B.
30.3% net margin, 18% revenue growth, 29.8% net income growth, and low $14.79B debt make this a solid compounder; margin sustainability is the key watch item.
Revenue $143.76B with 29.3% net margin is solid but $88.50B in total debt and only 15.9% net income growth relative to scale temper enthusiasm; need to see deleveraging.
Largest revenue base at $213.39B but only 9.9% net margin and 5.9% net income growth suggest limited operating leverage; would turn constructive if margins expand above 12%.
28.4% net margin is decent but net income declined 7% YoY and $435.21B in total debt (financial institution) makes the leverage profile hard to compare; need segment detail.
19.4% net margin is respectable but 1.5% revenue growth and -6.7% net income decline signal stagnation; would need re-acceleration to get constructive.
18% revenue growth is encouraging but net income fell 13.9% and 12.5% margin with $36.21B debt suggests cost pressures are eating into growth; need margin inflection.
Revenue declining 1.3% with net income down 14.6% on a thin 7.9% margin and $34.24B debt is a deteriorating earnings profile I refuse to pay for.
Net income collapsed 99.8% to near zero on $113.22B revenue — margin went to 0.0% despite 12.3% top-line growth, signaling severe cost or impairment issues.

memos.headline: Fed on Pause at 3.75% With Benign Inflation and Stable Labor Market — Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth, Neutral Banks
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in a pause regime: the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the past year, CPI is running at 2.4% y/y, and unemployment ticked down to 4.30% — a labor market that is softening only marginally. The 10y yield at 4.31% has risen 13 bps over three months while the 10y-2y spread compressed to 0.51 pp, suggesting the market is pricing a longer pause and modest term premium rebuild rather than imminent easing. This is a mid-cycle pause environment: growth is not accelerating but not rolling over, which favors quality duration-sensitive growth and is neutral-to-positive for cyclicals, while banks face margin headwinds from a flattening curve. A CPI print above 3% or unemployment jumping above 4.5% would force me to revisit this call — the former toward a hawkish re-pricing, the latter toward recession positioning.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from a stable-to-lower rate environment with the Fed on pause after 75 bps of cuts and benign 2.4% inflation.
Cyclicals are supported by a labor market holding near 4.3% unemployment and no imminent recession signal from the positively sloped yield curve.
Banks face headwinds from a 13 bp compression in the 10y-2y spread over three months, limiting net interest margin expansion despite a positive curve.
Staples lack a catalyst in a mid-cycle pause; neither recession fears nor rate cuts are accelerating enough to drive a defensive rotation.
Growth-oriented names benefit from the Fed's completed 75 bps easing cycle and stable real rates with inflation at 2.4%.
Energy lacks a clear macro tailwind; stable growth and no fiscal impulse signal keep me sidelined pending further data.

memos.headline: S03 and S09 Show Elevated Filing Activity Suggesting Narrative Shifts; S10 Post-Earnings Negativity May Be Washing Out
memos.body: I am reading the 8-K filing cadence and event types across the universe as a proxy for media/disclosure intensity and sentiment direction. S03 stands out with four filings since late February—including a material definitive agreement on 2/27 and a Reg FD disclosure just yesterday (4/9)—suggesting an active corporate narrative that could be turning positive if the company is proactively engaging investors. S10 took a -5.5% hit on its 2/25 earnings release and then saw a leadership change filing on 3/6; the negative tone may now be largely priced after six weeks, creating a potential mean-reversion setup. S05 has had two director departure/appointment filings in a month (3/6 and 4/2), which I read as board-level churn—a cautionary signal until the dust settles. S09 has three filings including a Reg FD on 4/8, indicating management is actively shaping the narrative, which I view as mildly constructive.

views.note: Unusually high filing cadence including a material agreement and fresh Reg FD disclosure suggests management is front-footing a positive narrative shift.
The -5.5% earnings-day drop on 2/25 and subsequent leadership change likely priced in the negativity; tone should be bottoming after six weeks.
Two director departure/appointment filings within a month signal board instability, a negative sentiment overhang until clarity emerges.
Three filings including a recent Reg FD suggest active investor engagement, but without clear positive catalysts I stay neutral.
Back-to-back officer changes in late Feb/early Mar and a Reg FD on 3/9 are ambiguous; not enough directional signal to take a stance.
Single Reg FD filing in late February with no follow-up activity leaves the sentiment picture stale and uninformative.

memos.headline: WTI at $99.62 (+69% in 3 months) signals a structural energy-security shock; policy uncertainty still elevated despite recent pullback
memos.body: I am reading the macro backdrop as dominated by a major energy supply disruption: WTI crude has surged 69% over three months to $99.62/bbl, a move consistent with sanctions escalation, supply-route disruption, or coordinated OPEC+ action rather than a simple demand story. The economic policy uncertainty index at 293.55 remains 27% above its level three months ago even after a sharp one-month decline of 39%, suggesting the acute phase of a policy shock may be fading but the structural overhang persists. High-yield OAS at 2.90% has tightened 29 bps over the past month, indicating credit markets are not yet pricing recession, but the 3-month widening of 16 bps and the flattening yield curve (10y-2y at 0.51 pp, down 13 bps over 3 months) tell me the bond market sees growth risk building. I have moderate conviction that energy-exposed names benefit while companies with high input-cost sensitivity or geopolitically concentrated supply chains face headwinds; a reversal in WTI below $80 or a de-escalation in policy uncertainty below 200 would change my view.

views.note: Four 8-K filings in six weeks including two Reg FD disclosures suggest active investor communication amid uncertainty, but without content detail I cannot take a directional view.
Back-to-back 8-Ks in late March and early April (including Reg FD) flag potential material developments, but the elevated policy uncertainty environment warrants caution until content is clearer.
With WTI near $100 and policy uncertainty elevated, companies sensitive to energy input costs face margin pressure; S05's single 8-K in February offers no offsetting positive signal.
February Reg FD disclosure is stale and the macro picture—tightening credit spreads but surging oil—creates offsetting forces; I lack enough firm-specific information to lean either way.
March Reg FD filing is the only firm-specific data point; the flattening curve and elevated oil prices create an ambiguous backdrop for S02.
If S07 has energy-sector exposure, the 69% three-month surge in WTI is a powerful tailwind; the March 8-K may relate to asset or operational updates that could crystallize value.
